title: Internal Hom under intrinsic finite-coefficient realization
statement: Let X be a scheme and A a finite commutative ring. Let R be the exact constant-scalar associated-module-sheaf realization on the small pro-etale site [def-sp-finite-coefficient-intrinsic-derived-comparison]. For arbitrary unbounded fixed-scalar derived complexes K,L, there exists an isomorphism R(RHom(K,L)) ≅ RHom(R(K),R(L)), where the left internal Hom is the fixed-ModuleCat pro-etale closed derived Hom and the right internal Hom is the recorded intrinsic Hom-complex localization [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. No constructibility, boundedness, separatedness, or nonempty-site hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: section-internal-hom, lemma-RHom-well-defined (Tag 0A95), and lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; coefficient-presentation transport in Step 2 of lem-sf-tensor-exchange-ctf-domains

proof.text: The realization is an exact equivalence with inverse restriction along the constant-scalar unit. On every slice the two tensors are the same sheafified balanced tensor, so the sheaf-Hom adjunction identifies the ordinary internal Homs.

An exact equivalence preserves acyclic complexes and K-injectivity. Apply realization to a K-injective representative of L; the ordinary Hom identifications identify the Hom complexes, products, and signed differentials. They therefore compute both recorded derived Homs.

Independence of K-injective representatives and the localization universal property extend this identification to arbitrary derived inputs, giving the asserted isomorphism. The zero-ring and empty-site cases use the same equivalence.

        (derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{u + 1, u, u} (ProEt.topology X)
          (proEtaleConstantRing X A)).obj
          (op ((finiteCoefficientIntrinsicRealization X A).mapDerivedCategory.obj K),
            (finiteCoefficientIntrinsicRealization X A).mapDerivedCategory.obj L))
